subject: Contingency & rollout controls for SLA breach — proposed policy
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected P99 spike after Friday deploy

Rishi —

Quick heads up: after your Friday push we started seeing P99 latency creep up on the inference route used by our billing flow. Baseline P99 was ~380ms, and we’ve observed sustained 1.1–1.4s spikes and a brief uptick in 5xxs (~0.6% over a 20m window). This is causing queued requests to pile up in our service and one of our downstream batch jobs missed its SLA today.

Can Redwood put an immediate mitigation in place? We need either a rolling rollback or an automatic fallback to the previous model variant while you investigate. Our contract (SLA section 3.2) expects 99th percentile latency under 500ms for this route.

If you can outline a short contingency plan (who will own the rollback and how long it will take) that would help us communicate to our ops team.

Thanks —
Olivia
Platform Reliability Manager
Acme Corp

Attachment: sample-error-log.txt (text stub)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@acme.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected P99 spike after Friday deploy

Olivia —

Thanks for the alert and the logs. I’m escalating this to engineering and ops now. Short answer: we can put an automated fallback and pin to the last stable model within ~15–30 minutes, and we’ll open a canary rollback run immediately.

Immediate plan (short):
- Trigger hot rollback to pinned model (rwd-model-v3.1-stable) as an automated fallback route.
- Start a controlled canary/AB re-deploy with strict rollback triggers (see next email).
- Marissa from support will coordinate communications; Laura will approve any SLA credit conversation if needed.

I’ll follow up with the internal runbook & triggers now.

— Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposal: automated canary/A-B policy as SLA contingency (draft)

Team —

Summary: Acme triggered a legitimate SLA impact after Friday’s model push. They’ve asked for a contingency plan we can execute immediately and standardize for future releases. Below is a proposed policy we can apply as an official SLA mitigation mechanism (will live in the runbook and be hooked into the control plane):

Policy (high level):
- Canary ramp: 5% traffic for 30m -> 25% for 1h -> 60% for 2h -> 100% if metrics stable.
- Canary checks (must pass to progress):
  * P99 latency for route under 500ms (threshold configurable per-route).
  * Error rate (5xx + client 4xx errors relevant to model) under 0.5% over rolling 10m window.
  * No CPU/GPU saturation signal (>90%) and queuing depth under 30 requests.
- Automatic fallback & pin: If any check violates thresholds for two consecutive 10m windows, system pins routing to the last-stable model id (metadata: rwd-model-v3.1-stable) and shifts 100% traffic to pinned variant.
- Forced rollback window: rollback will be executed automatically if violation persists for 10m. Engineers will be paged; if rollback cannot be performed automatically (e.g., infra issue), we fall back to region-level routing to a different capacity pool.
- Canary duration & review: keep canary logs; runbook requires a post-mortem and, for customer-impacting incidents, an SLA credit assessment.

Triggers & escalation:
- Pager to on-call infra + rwd-release (aditya.rao) if P99 > 750ms or 5xx > 0.5% for 10 minutes.
- If rollback occurs, Marissa to open a customer incident summary; Laura to approve any credits.

Operational notes:
- We need a small UI affordance in the console to manually pin/unpin model versions and to force the fallback immediately.
- Add an opt-in per-account field: "allow-auto-fallback" (default false). For customers under SLA (like Acme) we’ll enable it by default and record consent in the contract amendments.

Action items (owners):
- Aditya: implement the short-circuit auto-pin in control plane and add webhook to publish rollback events to Jira (INF-6324).
- Marissa: brief Acme on immediate rollback window and own customer comms.
- Laura: approve temporary activation of auto-fallback for Acme and sign off on any credit policy.

I’ve attached the initial SLO threshold doc and a lightweight canary runbook. Please review — we should be ready to execute now.

Rishi

Attachment: canary_runbook.md, slo_thresholds.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 17:42:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: automated canary/A-B policy as SLA contingency (draft)

Thanks — reviewed and approved for emergency activation for Acme. A few clarifications before we flip the switch:

1) Threshold margins: set hard rollback triggers at P99 >= 750ms and soft-alert at P99 >= 600ms so on-call has early visibility.
2) Consent log: Marissa, get a written confirmation from Olivia that Acme accepts auto-fallback behavior; copy legal if they ask for contract verbiage.
3) Telemetry retention: keep 1 week of high-resolution canary telemetry (per route) and 90 days of aggregated metrics.

Aditya: can you prioritize the control-plane pin endpoint and webhook today? If implementation risk is high, we’ll perform the fallback via manual ops steps (runbook has checklist).

Marissa: I’ll approve a one-time SLA credit if needed after post-mortem. Coordinate with finance.

Once Aditya confirms the pin endpoint, Rishi you can authorize the automatic fallback for ACME and execute the canary ramp.

Laura
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
